newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-India shares surge two pct as Gujral made PM.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-India shares surge two pct as Gujral made PM.

text.p: Indian stock markets surged two percent on Monday as a prolonged political crisis was defused after a new Prime Minister was sworn in, analysts said.
"It's business as before," said Amit Prahladka, vice president at Reliance Capital Asset Management Ltd.
"The parties are virtually the same and there are unlikely to be any major changes in the cabinet."
New prime minister, Inder Kumar Gujral, retained the cabinet of his predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, except for Finance Minister P.Chidamabaram and four other departing ministers.
Returning ministers will keep the same portfolios, and there was speculation that Chidambaram could be wooed back on board.

Gujral -- who was sworn in on Monday at the head of a centre-left government supported by the Congress party -- said he would press ahead with open-market economic reforms pursued by the two previous governments.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index jumped 70.15 points, or 1.9 percent, to 3766.67 in afternoon trade -- slightly off the day's high of 3771.82.

Shares on the Bombay-based National Stock Exchange and on other regional bourses like Calcutta gained more than one percent. But on the Delhi bourse, stocks fell slightly as investors remained cautious.
Stock markets across the country were volatile during the crisis triggered by the Congress party's shock decision last month to withdraw vital support to the ruling coalition.
Gujral told reporters after taking the oath of office that he would keep the foreign and finance ministry portfolios for himself in the new centre-left government.
Investors interpreted this as a sign that outgoing Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) was likely to rejoin the new government.

"The market has taken this news very favourably," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, an affiliate of U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs. "This could only mean that the government is expecting a reconciliation with the TMC."

The TMC, miffed that its leader G.K. Moopanar was not chosen to lead the United Front, said on Saturday that it would not join the government but would lend support to the alliance from outside. But Gujral said he was hopeful the TMC would join his government.
"The fact that Gujral has kept the finance portfolio means he's still negotiating with TMC," said Keshav Sanghi, equities salesman at HSBC James Capel in Hong Kong.

"Hopefully Gujral will manage to convince Moopanar to come back and you'll see some sort of compromise. The picture will will get a lot clearer once the vote of confidence and the budget go through," Sanghi said.
Gujral is due to face a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT).
Parliament is due to take up the budget proposals for 1997/98 (April-March) after it reassembles on April 30.
"Temporarily things seem to be settled," said the head of sales at a European brokerage. "We're recommending people stay invested and are asking them to stick to pivotals."
But he said prices were likely to trade narrowly in the coming month as investors turned their attention to upcoming financial results for 1996/97.
India's top private firm Reliance Industries is due to announce its results on Tuesday and analysts have forecast a slight fall in net profit due to lower global petrochemicals prices.
--Bombay newsroom, (91) 22 265 9000
